newsitem.title: UK: Treasuries steady in London, triple witching looms.
newsitem.headline: Treasuries steady in London, triple witching looms.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries in London were broadly steady to slightly firmer amid quiet trade, although traders said they were looking for more action at the end of the week.
Friday's quarterly expiration of options, index options and futures -- known as triple witching -- is expected to add increased volatility to the market.

"Things are dead at the moment," said a trader at a French bank in London. "But we've got triple witching on Friday and since the futures were struggling to get over 113-00, I can see them heading back to 112-00."
The U.S. 30-year Treasury bond was trading at 98-00, yielding 6.65 percent, compared with 98-01 in Tokyo and 97-28 in New York. March T-bond futures were down 1/32 at 112-16 in automated trade.
Traders said they expected the two-year auction of Treasuries to be well received, although there was more chance that Thursday's five-year auction could unsettle the market.
The U.S. Treasury will sell $18.5 billion of two-year notes later on Wednesday, followed by $12.5 billion of five-year notes on Thursday.
"People are hoping there will be some interest out of Asia," said the French bank trader.
He said recent reports that Japanese investors were ceasing the buy U.S. debt assets were viewed as unlikely, and even if true, would not be a single, dramatic move.
"It's not like turning a tap off, but more like trying to stop a supertanker," the trader said.
There was no major economic data scheduled for release in the U.S.
